problem: A game show uses a roulette wheel divided into $50$ panels. There are $15$ blue, $15$ green, $15$ yellow, $2$ black, and $3$ white panels randomly shuffled on the roulette wheel. What is the probability that the roulette wheel stops on a white or green panel?

feedback.problem: Suppose that $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events. Given that $P(B)=\frac{8}{21}$ and $P(A\cup B)=\frac{3}{4},$ find $P(A).$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events, then $P(A\cap B)=0.$ 

Therefore, by the addition law, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B) \\ P(A) & =P(A\cup B)-P(B) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}-\frac{8}{21} \\  & =\frac{63-32}{84} \\  & =\frac{31}{84}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
